subject: Request: FalconTech compute-reservation API for enterprise SLA
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Joshua Park <joshua.park@falcontech.com>, Leah Gomez <leah.gomez@falcontech.com>, FalconTech Contracts <contracts@falcontech.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: FalconTech compute-reservation API for enterprise SLA

Team —

Quick summary: FalconTech is finalizing a multi-year commitment (see attached MAP + SOW redlines). They require a programmatic way to reserve dedicated compute capacity for critical windows (business hours plus scheduled batch windows) with an API we can surface to their platform team. The ask is framed as a gating SLA item: guaranteed request-level latency and no cold-start degradation during reserved windows.

Why this matters for the deal:
- Falcon is asking for a written capability in the SOW that we can reliably hit (they will seek credits for misses).
- This is a >$2M ARR contract with strong references and a fast close timeline (legal wants signature this quarter).

What I need from Product/Eng (high level):
1) Feasibility: can we expose a compute-reservation API (reserve N slots for a tenant for a time window) without a full infra rewrite?
2) Scope: what level of guarantee do we realistically provide (concurrency, p50/p95 latency, model variants supported)?
3) Risk & timeline: rough engineering effort and earliest ship date for an MVP we could commit to in the SOW.

Files attached: FalconTech_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (customer timeline) and SOW-v2-redlines.pdf (legal redlines).

Asking for a short sync tomorrow (30m) to align on what we can promise. If we can’t support the API exactly, please propose alternatives we could include in the SOW (e.g., dedicated pool reservation + SLAs, advance capacity booking via support playbook, or a managed warm-cache runbook).

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: FalconTech compute-reservation API for enterprise SLA

Marissa —

Thanks for the context. Technical takeaways from SE POV:
- We already support Dedicated GPU pools (Reserved capacity) with configuration for min/max nodes. Exposing programmatic reservation is feasible as a thin orchestration layer that ties an API call to allocation in the existing scheduler.
- Major gaps:
  • Fine-grained per-tenant slot reservation across multi-model catalogs (different model sizes) needs allocation-by-queue changes.
  • SLA enforcement + automated crediting on misses requires instrumentation and billing integration (we lack an automated 'SLA metering' pipeline).
- Quick workaround (low risk, faster): Offer a documented reserved-pool + guaranteed pre-warm procedure: customer requests windows via our support API, we allocate nodes and run a warm-up job during window start. This delivers most customer-facing guarantees but is manual/operationally heavier.

Estimated dev effort for MVP full API: 6-8 wks (1 eng + 1 infra + 0.5 QA FTE) if we scope to a single model family and attach simple metering. SLA metering + billing integration adds 3-4 wks.

I can demo a prototype scheduler change this week if helpful.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Marissa / Ben —

Thanks — this is helpful. A few product questions to clarify scope before we propose a commitment in the SOW:
1) Single vs multi-model: Do they require the reservation to span multiple model sizes (e.g., Llama-70B + smaller LLMs) or will they accept guarantees scoped to a specific instance type?
2) Window granularity: Are windows recurring (daily business hours) or ad-hoc reserved windows for launches? Recurring reservations have easier scheduler guarantees.
3) Failover behavior: If we can't satisfy the reservation (hardware failure / oversubscription), do they expect automatic fallback to hosted model variants? If so, what's acceptable latency degradation?

Once we have answers I can sketch a minimal product commitment (e.g., "reserved pool of X GPUs for Y hours per day for primary model family; p95 latency target N ms; manual on-call escalation path"), and indicate the required acceptance criteria for the SOW.

Priyom
Product Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: FalconTech compute-reservation API for enterprise SLA

Hi Marissa / team —

Answers inline to help scope:
1) Multi-model: We need the reservation to cover 1 primary production model (Falcon-Prod-70B) and a small set (<=2) of smaller models for bursts. It’s OK to call this a "primary model family" in the SOW.
2) Window granularity: Both. We need a recurring business-hours reservation (Mon-Fri 9am-6pm PT) plus the ability to reserve additional ad-hoc blocks for launches (typically 2-6 hour windows).
3) Failover: Acceptable fallback is a model variant with up to 2x p95 latency, but only during rare, well-documented failovers; any downgrade must be accompanied by credits if it exceeds the agreed p95.

We'd like to avoid manual runbooks for the daily business-hours guarantee — that undermines their compliance ask.

Thanks,
Josh
Director, Platform Engineering | FalconTech

Folks —

Security/compliance notes to factor into the product commitment:
- Isolation: If we provision dedicated GPU capacity, we need to confirm tenant isolation controls and audit logs for allocation + access. FalconTech will request evidence during procurement (audit artifacts).
- Key handling: Any automated reservation mechanism that triggers model loading must not persist customer keys in plaintext; KMS integration needs to be documented if we automate warm-up.
- Playbook for failover: The SOW must include an incident response step with RTO expectations and an owner in our on-call rota.

I can supply a short "security appendix" that we can attach to the SOW if Product agrees to the capability surface.

—Stephanie
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Team —

Thanks for the rapid input. Two asks to close this week so legal can finalize the SOW: 
1) Product decision: can we commit to an MVP whose scope is: recurring reservation for a single primary model family (Falcon-Prod-70B family), Mon-Fri 9-6 PT, up to N concurrent reserved slots (TBD), with on-call escalation and documented incident response? If yes, provide the minimal acceptance criteria (exact p95 target, supported model variants, and the time-to-restore clause) we can put in the SOW.
2) Security appendix: Stephanie, please prepare the short appendix and list the evidence items FalconTech can request (audit logs, allocation history).

If Product cannot accept this scope, suggest the fallback we present to the customer (dedicated reserved pool + automated warm-up script run by our ops team, with a support SLA).

I'll push for a 11am PT sync tomorrow if you can make it. Falcon's procurement is pushing for final language before EOD Friday.

Thanks —
